sources.cite: 8. Errors and Exceptions, The Python Tutorial, Python 3.15 documentation
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-16. Relevant text: 'The last line of the error message indicates what happened. Exceptions come in different types, and the type is printed as part of the message'; 'A try statement may have more than one except clause, to specify handlers for different exceptions. At most one handler will be executed'; 'Exception can be used as a wildcard that catches (almost) everything. However, it is good practice to be as specific as possible with the types of exceptions that we intend to handle, and to allow any unexpected exceptions to propagate on'; the common pattern is to 'print or log the exception and then re-raise it'. The tutorial does not discuss a bare except: as such; the case's bare-except trap rests on the same advice. The traceback and error text in the case are authored renderings in CPython's style.
